notable_absence.finding: There are no try/catch blocks and only limited error checking in this handler, by the page's own admission ('There are no try catch blocks and only limited error checking to highlight the functionality') - no Eventing-specific error-handling primitive is documented or exercised here.

cross_component_finding: supersedesTimerReference (minted for the control-document pause/cancel/overwrite pattern in eventing-examples-cancel-overwrite-timer.json) reappears here for a structurally different trigger - the handler itself repeatedly calling createTimer with the same notifyId on every mutation of the same shipping document - confirming this is a general Timer-identity behavior (same reference id supersedes the pending Timer), not tied to the control-document pattern specifically.
cross_product_finding: The "notify" collection is explicitly framed as an integration point with systems outside Eventing: "The \"notify\"collection can be used to integrate with SDK or Kafka to send notifications." This names a third-party system (Kafka) and the Couchbase SDK as downstream consumers of Eventing's output via a staging collection, rather than describing a dedicated Eventing notification feature.
